summary: C26 composes the existing C14/C16 boundaries into one fixture-driven resilience scenario: a signed-bounded offline spool drops beyond its limit with one durable gap and loss summary, duplicate batch delivery returns identical receipts without duplicate observations, a real store restart preserves revision, receipts, acknowledgements and loss accounting, and delivery continues across the explicit gap. Seven typed negative batches leave the store unchanged, and the composed path imports no network capability. The real rootless-container egress anchor and the C14/C16 SIGKILL anchors ran in the same 192-anchor required suite. Full Go race, npm check and contracts checks passed locally.
hosted_actions_note: Not run for this source. No push or publication occurred; remote workflow status is unverified.
scope_limits: Local Linux process and filesystem proofs only; no physical power-loss, multi-host or consensus claim.
Container egress and crash recovery remain the existing C13/C14/C16 anchors; C26 does not duplicate them.
Fixture bounds (spool_limit_events=3, event_batch_limit=2) are test policy, not product defaults or measured capacity.
No browser run because no web source changed; web regressions remain with the unchanged workflow.
No production code, schema, migration, .env, Dockerfile, dependency or storage format changed.
C28 measurements, full C30 restart/restore and C40 release remain pending.
